description: Analyze a render or audio file: loudness, spectrum, envelope, stereo. See describe for errors and examples.

detail.description: summary: key scalars; standard: + percentiles and spectrum; full: + time series.

name: batch
title: Run commands atomically.
description: Run commands atomically. See describe for errors and examples.

name: branch_create
title: Start a branch from a head or an earlier version and switch to it.
description: Agents: work on agent/<you>/<topic> branches, then branch.diff and branch.merge into main. Merging replays your edits onto main even if main moved; conflicting edits are reported. See describe for errors and examples.

version.description: Start at this version of the current branch's history (history.list; a render result's version) instead of a head

name: branch_diff
title: What differs between two branch heads: added, removed, changed objects.
description: What differs between two branch heads: added, removed, changed objects. See describe for errors and examples.

name: branch_merge
title: Merge a branch into another (default: main) by replaying its edits.
description: Fast-forwards when the target has not moved. Otherwise replays the branch's edits; IDs it created are renumbered where needed (see remapped). If both sides changed the same field of an object, nothing is merged and the error lists each conflict. See describe for errors and examples.

name: branch_switch
title: Make another branch current (edits, undo and playback follow it).
description: Make another branch current (edits, undo and playback follow it). See describe for errors and examples.

name: engine_start
title: Start playback through JACK, native PortAudio, or a device-free dummy.
description: backend: jack (Linux default), portaudio (macOS/Windows native device), or dummy (default elsewhere, no device). For portaudio, host_api, input_device and output_device select exact names from engine.devices. inputs defaults to 0 (playback only); outputs (the device channels masters can play to, track.set hw_output) defaults to one per physical playback port with JACK (2 to 64) and 2 otherwise. rate defaults to the project rate; a rate given is asked of the device (CoreAudio switches the device's rate when it can, WASAPI converts) or, with JACK on PipeWire, suggested to the graph (node.rate: applied only while the devices are idle and the rate is allowed). force_graph (JACK on PipeWire, default false) instead forces block as the graph's quantum, and rate if given, while the engine runs. PortAudio opens up to 16 native MIDI inputs and outputs; engine.inputs lists their names. Dummy is paced like a device. block: the device block in frames (default 256); the device's period may differ and is reported. anticipative (default true): render ahead of the playhead on worker threads (edits are heard up to 200 ms later); false renders everything in the audio callback. The engine runs at the device's rate (media is resampled; renders stay at the project's rate). Background and live thread capacities follows the app's Audio processing threads preference (Automatic by default); live helpers join each callback with no added latency. memory_lock reports the default-off host-process memory policy: requested, active, and a structured OS error on failure. cpu_idle_latency reports the 20 microsecond PM QoS request: requested by the default-off option, or automatic, held on Linux while a bridged plug-in plays live; released on engine stop. thp_opt_out: on Linux the process is kept out of transparent huge pages while the engine runs (advised_only: regions a plug-in advised keep them). A protection failure does not prevent audio startup. MIDI output refusals are in midi_output_warnings; midi_output_latency reports signed audio-minus-MIDI frames per output. MIDI inputs that refuse to open are skipped: midi_warnings reports each device, numeric os_error, message and corrective hint; audio continues. See describe for errors and examples.

name: env_add
title: Automate a parameter: a track's or route's mixer control, or a plugin's.
description: Target one of track (param volume|pan|mute; width|pan_left|pan_right|pan_boost on channels/busses; playrate only on tr_0), route (volume|pan|mute), group (VCA volume|mute), or fx (a semantic key such as "gain" or "filter1.cutoff", or for other plugins a CLAP id or parameter name; a semantic plugin's parameter named by id or name is stored by its key, its plain points converted to the key's units: converted), or module (a rack module's knob by key, values in its unit, a choice by its key; module.describe). points: [{beat|bar|seconds, value, shape?, tension?}]; values in the parameter's unit (dB, %, Hz… — text like "800 Hz" works for plugins); shapes linear, square, slow, fast_start, fast_end, bezier. Plugin values move along the parameter's curve (a log cutoff sweeps evenly in pitch). take (param volume|pan|mute): a take envelope, its points in beats from the item's start (it moves with the item), or on a clip's take from the clip's start in beats (MIDI) or seconds (audio); it shapes the take after its take FX (a MIDI take needs an instrument in its take FX). Master playrate points are finite numeric ratios 0.25..4.0; an active nonempty master curve replaces the saved scalar during playback and rendering. Audio sources convert before take FX/live mixing; MIDI and automation follow the same timeline clock. Width and dual pans use -100..100 percent; pan_boost uses 0..1 (on at 0.5), overriding the effective law's boost while the envelope is active and nonempty. See describe for errors and examples.

name: env_points_set
title: Replace an envelope's points (all of them, or those in a beat range).
description: from_beat/to_beat: replace only points with from_beat <= beat < to_beat. On a clip's take or take FX they are in the clip's unit from its start (beats, or seconds on an audio clip). See describe for errors and examples.

name: fx_add
title: Insert a plugin into a track's (or a take's) FX chain and return its id.
description: plugin: id or name from plugin.list; patch: an initial (partial) patch for semantic plugins. chain: main (default; the track's effects) or input (the recorded-input chain). take instead of track: the take's own chain (take FX) — the item plays through it before the track's input, cut to the item; an instrument there plays a MIDI take on its own. An instrument with outputs past its main pair (a multi-out sampler's Kick, Snare...) gets that many more channels on the track, and its pins.out sends each output there; route.matrix lists them and route.add {channels: {from: [3, 4]}} sends one to a buss. Without index, a note effect (an arpeggiator) goes to the front of the track's chain, ahead of what it plays, and an instrument after the note effects there. See describe for errors and examples.

name: fx_describe
title: Describe an instance and its live problems; full adds parameters and patch.
description: Describe an instance and its live problems; full adds parameters and patch. See describe for errors and examples.

filter.description: Plain parameters only: list those whose name contains this text (case-insensitive).

name: fx_patch_get
title: Read a semantic plugin's saved patch.
description: Read a semantic plugin's saved patch. See describe for errors and examples.

name: fx_patch_merge
title: Merge a partial patch into a plugin instance; returns the effective change.
description: Semantic plugins only. Values in physical units: {"params": {"gain": "-6 dB"}}. changed holds only the members the merge changed: against the saved patch, or for an instance never saved against the plug-in's defaults (a value set to what it already is changes nothing). See describe for errors and examples.

name: fx_remove
title: Remove a plugin instance (and its envelopes).
description: Remove a plugin instance (and its envelopes). See describe for errors and examples.

name: history_undo
title: Undo the last change on the current branch.
description: Steps the current branch back one version. The result is the version that is current afterwards and its label: the step before the one undone, not the undone step (history.list shows both). See describe for errors and examples.

name: item_add
title: Add an item on a track: notation, a MIDI or audio file, or a clip's copy.
description: position in beats (quarter notes from the start) or bar (1-based). notation: e.g. "voice bass; 1: C2:q r:q C2:q r:q | F2:h G2:h" — every bar must add up; the item is as long as the written bars unless length (beats) is given. audio_file: a path at the project's sample rate; with the app's copy-imports setting on, the project keeps its own copy in its media folder. midi_file: a Standard MIDI File (type 0 or 1, every track merged, channels kept); its notes keep their beats and follow the project's tempo (the file's tempo and meter are not applied; a warning says when they differ), and the item is as long as the file unless length is given. clip: a copy of that clip's takes, as long as the clip, its loop and take envelopes converted at the tempo where the item lands (ADR-0097); the item is named as the clip is (its active take's name) when the clip has a name. follow (none, key or chords; default: the clip's own) maps the clip's notes from the key or chords it was written against to those under the item (ADR-0098): notes on channel 10 and clips that cannot follow are copied, and the answer's followed says what was done, by bar. With none the notes are copied as they are and context.mismatch warns when the clip's key, or in the same key its chord, is not the project's under the item. A master holds audio items only (prints, played after its fader); busses hold none. See describe for errors and examples.

clip.description: Lay a copy of this clip's takes here.

follow.description: How the clip's notes are mapped to the key (or chords) under the item (ADR-0098): none, key or chords. Default: the clip's own follow.

name: item_remove
title: Remove an item with its takes (unpooled sources go too).
description: Remove an item with its takes (unpooled sources go too). See describe for errors and examples.

item.description: Item id, e.g. "it_1" (a clip's id is refused with item.kind).

name: item_set
title: Set an item's position, length, playback, fades, name, color, or lock.
description: Positions and lengths are in beats; fades are in seconds. Name is the active take's name. A locked item refuses every edit except {"locked": false}. timebase: what the item follows when the tempo changes — beats (moves and stretches with it), time (stays at its seconds), beats_position (its start follows the beat, its length stays in seconds) or track (inherit); the item keeps its place now. See describe for errors and examples.

item.description: Item id, e.g. "it_1" (a clip's id is refused with item.kind).

locked.description: The arrange view marks locked items.

gain_db.description: Quantity strings are range-checked by the server. (dB; accepts quantity strings)

name: midi_get
title: Read an item's or clip's MIDI as notation, with its key and chords.
description: Pitch names follow the key that holds at the item's start (none: the default spelling). context lists the key and the chords over the item's span, each from the bar of the item (item_bar, the notation's) and of the project (project_bar) where it starts; the first of each is the one already holding at the item's start. Omitted when the project has no key or chords there. A clip has no place in time: its pitch names follow its own key at its start, and its context is the key and chords it was written against: runs by clip bar (item_bar, no project_bar) and beat from its start, and text, its lead sheet in clip bars (clip.set {context} takes it back). follow (none, key, chords) is a clip's. See describe for errors and examples.

item.description: Item or clip id, e.g. "it_1" or "cl_1".

name: midi_write
title: Replace an item's or clip's MIDI with notation (keeping its place and length).
description: The item or clip keeps its length: notation longer than it is stored but does not play past its end, and midi.beyond_length warns. Lengthen it first (item.set length, clip.set length), or write the notation to fit. See describe for errors and examples.

item.description: Item or clip id, e.g. "it_1" or "cl_1".

name: modulate
title: Modulate a parameter or mixer level: LFO, follower, random, macro.
description: The whole gesture in one undo step. It takes the first rack homed on the target's track that holds a Mod Out, else the first rack named Modulators, else adds one on a new channel named Modulators (rack: choose one instead). It adds the source module (lfo: an LFO; random: an LFO's Random Steps preset; macro: a Macro, its first knob; follower: a Follower fed by an In module and a send from the track from), cables it into the first free Mod Out input (adding a Mod Out when none is free) and routes that input to the target. {module, input} routes a Mod Out input already patched. For a macro, knob names the knob to move. depth as modulation.add; default a quarter of a plug-in parameter's range, 6 dB, or 50 percent. A parameter reached through its envelope (fx.describe: modulatable_by_envelope) gets a one-point envelope at its current value first when it has none. A rack that would close a loop (it already drives the track a follower hears, or hears the target) is passed over for the next, or a new Modulators rack. Only a real cycle is refused (modulation.cycle): a follower on a track the target feeds, itself included. target: {fx, param} (a plug-in parameter by key, name or CLAP id; fx.describe full marks the modulatable ones), {track, param: volume|pan|width} or {route, param: volume}. The source module is left set to its defaults: change it with module.set {module, params} on the module this returns (an LFO's rate, shape or sync; a follower's gain and threshold; a macro's macro_1, which sits at 0 until moved, so a macro does nothing at first; module.describe {type} lists the knobs) and the route's depth with modulation.set. A second route from the same kind of source onto a target that already has one warns modulation.stacked (their offsets add). See describe for errors and examples.

track.description: A track's volume, pan or width.

param.description: A plug-in parameter's key, name or decimal CLAP id (fx.describe marks the modulatable ones); volume, pan or width for a track; volume for a route.

from.description: The track a follower listens to.

name: plugin_list
title: List scanned plugins; filter matches id, name, or vendor.
description: List scanned plugins; filter matches id, name, or vendor. See describe for errors and examples.

name: project_get
title: Show the project: name, rate, tempo, meter, file, version and branch.
description: recoverable: recordings a crash left out of the project (project.recoverable). autosave_available: a newer autosave exists next to the file; open it as a project if you want it (nothing is loaded silently). See describe for errors and examples.

name: project_open
title: Open a project file and its branches (replaces the current project).
description: recoverable > 0: recordings a crash left out of the project; project.recoverable lists them and project.recover puts them back. autosave_available: a newer autosave exists next to the file (it is not loaded silently). branch: the branch current when saved. warnings: project.history when the saved branches could not be restored (main opens alone; the first save over the file keeps a copy of it); also project module copies that could not be read or compiled, and name types using a library version instead or left unavailable; project.suspect_plugin when a crash report points at a plug-in the project holds (it loads normally: the engine never prompts or changes how a plug-in loads by itself; plugin.override first to protect the run). See describe for errors and examples.

expect_hash.description: The hash project.plugins returned: the file is opened only if its bytes are those it checked (project.changed otherwise)

name: project_save
title: Save the project (canonical JSON) to its file or a new path.
description: path: where to save (becomes the project's file); omit to save in place. The file keeps every branch with its unmerged steps (undoable after opening) and which branch is current; history: true also keeps undo history. warnings: running plug-ins whose current state could not be read; the file keeps the state each had before (fx.restart, then save again, or replace the plug-in); project.history_backup names the copy kept of a file whose branches could not be restored when opened. project.recording: a first save, or a save into another folder, while recording; stop first. project.autosave_folder: the autosave folder beside the file (<file>-data) could not be read; nothing was written. See describe for errors and examples.

history.description: Also keep undo and redo history (ADR-0076)

name: render_mix
title: Render the mix offline with the project's settings (default: whole song).
description: Arguments override project.render (then the user's default, then built-ins) for this call only; render.settings shows what applies. Files go to the renders folder, named by pattern (subfolders allowed). job: true runs the render as a job (job.get for progress, job.cancel to stop). Each file lists its outputs (with delivery checks when a loudness target or a ceiling is set), branch, version, start_beat, seconds, a render id (analyze.render, analyze.compare) and an analysis summary. The mix answers with its file's entry at the top level (path, secondary_path, outputs, peak_dbfs, …); analyze: summary or full adds the report inline. masters renders several masters, a file each (the first on top, all in files); a pattern without {track} then gets -{track}, the master's name. See describe for errors and examples.

source.description: The dialog's source; render.mix always renders the mix

masters.description: The mix: the masters to render, a file each (default: tr_0)

pattern.description: File name pattern (session-model §7.3; may contain / for subfolders), for every source or as {mix, stems, regions}

items.title: render output
items.description: One encoding of the rendered audio

bit_depth.description: WAV 16/24/32 (float) [32]; AIFF and FLAC 16/24 [24]; none for MP3 and Vorbis

dither.description: 16- and 24-bit output: none, tpdf (default) or shaped

suffix.description: Inserted before the extension of a second or later output, e.g. "-16bit"

outputs.description: 1-4 encodings of the same audio [[{format: wav, bit_depth: 32}]]

scope.description: file (default), or master: stems share the master mix's gain

seamless_loop.description: Sum the tail into the start (needs tail_s)

handles_s.description: Regions: seconds added at both ends

mode.description: isolated (default; no master processing) or through_master

skip_silent.description: Leave out stems whose peak is below -90 dBFS

metadata.title: render metadata
metadata.description: Tags written into each file; text members accept the file-name tokens

cover.description: A PNG or JPEG of at most 10 MiB, relative to the project folder

bwf.description: WAV: a BWF bext chunk (v2) with time reference and loudness

markers.description: WAV cue points / AIFF markers for the markers and regions in the file's range

master.description: Mix: one master for this call (default: the settings' masters, else tr_0)

branch.description: Render this branch's head (default: the current one)

version.description: Render the session as of this version (history.list); the render queue pins its renders

name.description: A file name instead of the pattern, for this call

operation.description: Dry run and render.settings: mix, stems or regions (default: tracks or regions given, else the settings' source)

regions.description: Regions: region ids (default: all, with the render matrix)

tracks.description: Stems: track ids (sets stems.tracks for this call)

secondary.description: Replaces outputs[1] ({format, bit_depth}), or "none" removes it, for this call

name: route_add
title: Send audio between tracks, or MIDI between channels and rack modules.
description: The destination must not feed the source. Master accepts routes. With fx instead of to, the send feeds that plug-in's sidechain (key) input — e.g. a kick keying a compressor on the bass; it is delay-compensated, and soloing the keyed track does not stop the key. MIDI sends use channel or Note Out sources and channel or Notes destinations, midi: {} (all channels unchanged); from_channel filters and to_channel remaps, 0..16 with 0 meaning all/original. to_midi selects a hardware MIDI output by exact name instead of to. Missing outputs warn while audio keeps playing. A rack's Out module (from: mo_N) sends audio to a buss or master: a rack send, added after the destination's Console 9 decode, never encoded, with level and mute only; it follows the mute and solo of the rack's home channel (ADR-0075). See describe for errors and examples.

to_midi.description: Exact hardware MIDI output name; requires midi: {} and replaces to/fx.

midi.title: midi_routing
midi.description: MIDI send routing; {} means every channel unchanged. Channel values 0..16: from 0 = all, to 0 = original.

fx.description: Feed this plug-in's sidechain (key) input instead of a track's input; `to` may be left out

volume_db.description: Quantity strings are range-checked by the server. (dB; accepts quantity strings)

oneOf.description: Quantity strings are range-checked by the server.

mono.description: Sum the source to mono before the pan

channels.title: channel_map
channels.description: Which source channel feeds which destination channel, pair by pair: {from: [1, 2], to: [2, 1]} swaps, {from: [1, 1], to: [1, 2]} sends the left channel to both, {from: [], to: []} restores the identity

name: session_describe
title: Describe the session in compact text: tracks, items, fx, routes, key.
description: The quickest way to see where things are; use the IDs it shows with other commands. See describe for errors and examples.

name: tempo_set
title: Replace the tempo map: points {beat, bpm, ramp?}, the first at beat 0.
description: ramp: true changes the tempo linearly (in beats) to the next point; otherwise it steps. See describe for errors and examples.

bpm.description: Quantity strings are range-checked by the server.

name: track_add
title: Add a track (a channel, buss or master) and return its id.
description: parent: a buss/master id (default tr_0); masters have no parent; index: position among its siblings; name: default the first free ch_N, buss_N or mstr_N. A new channel gets the user's default monitoring (on unless set otherwise; monitoring needs the track armed). color: a track colour's name or "#rrggbb", "" for none; default for a channel or buss the palette colour the fewest tracks carry (red first), for a master none. See describe for errors and examples.

name: track_list
title: List tracks in tree order with their level, mute/solo, fx and items.
description: List tracks in tree order with their level, mute/solo, fx and items. See describe for errors and examples.

name: track_remove
title: Remove a track with its items, clips, fx, routes and envelopes (not a folder).
description: Removes the track's racks too, except a rack another channel hears (its Out as the channel's input, or its Note Out's MIDI), which moves there. A warning names each rack removed (track.rack_removed) or moved (track.rack_moved) and its rack sends: removed with it, or following the new home's mute and solo. Its clips go with their takes, named by a clip.removed warning. See describe for errors and examples.

name: track_set
title: Set track fields; choosing audio, MIDI or rack input replaces the others.
description: Only the given fields change. solo: off | on | in_place | defeat. armed + record_input (device input channels, 1-based) prepare a track for transport.record; record_midi records MIDI instead: hardware audio and MIDI or a rack Out (record_rack) replace each other: a track has one input. Choosing one clears the other kinds. null clears only the named kind; set all three to null for no input. Feed a rack's Notes through MIDI sends from another channel. A device name is a substring of the MIDI port ("*" = every device), with midi_channel 1-16 (0 = all). monitor: off | on | auto (auto: while armed) — a monitored track hears its input live (an instrument plays the keyboard), also while stopped. record_mode: input (new items), midi_overdub (merge into the MIDI item under the start, as a new take), midi_replace. color: red | orange | yellow | green | teal | blue | violet | grey | "#rrggbb" ("" clears it), shown as a stripe on the track. A master takes armed alone: transport.record then records its output (after its fader, before its own items) as an item on the master; lane_mute silences a master's items. chain_midi: bus (every plug-in with a note input hears the chain's MIDI, a note-output plug-in feeds those after it and the post-FX sends) or instrument (only the first such plug-in hears the track's MIDI, as before 2.10). See describe for errors and examples.

volume_db.description: Quantity strings are range-checked by the server. (dB; accepts quantity strings)

pan.description: Quantity strings are range-checked by the server. (%; accepts quantity strings)

pan_mode.description: Channels and busses: pan (balance a stereo image, pan a mono one), dual (pan_left and pan_right place each input on its own) or width (width narrows, widens or swaps the image, pan places it)

width.description: Width mode: 100 as recorded, 0 mono, -100 sides swapped Quantity strings are range-checked by the server. (%; accepts quantity strings)

pan_left.description: Dual mode: where the left input goes (default -100) Quantity strings are range-checked by the server. (%; accepts quantity strings)

pan_right.description: Dual mode: where the right input goes (default 100) Quantity strings are range-checked by the server. (%; accepts quantity strings)

anyOf.title: pan_law

db.description: Quantity strings are range-checked by the server.

anyOf.description: This track's pan law: db is the centre's cut (0, -2.5, -3, -4.5 or -6); boost raises the sides instead. null follows project.pan_law

phase_invert.description: Flip the polarity of the main pair (after the FX chain, before the fader)

mono.description: Sum the main pair to mono (after the FX chain, before the fader and pan): a mono check on the master

record_input.description: Hardware audio input; replaces MIDI or rack input. null clears hardware audio only

record_midi.description: MIDI device; replaces hardware audio or rack input. null clears MIDI only

anyOf.description: A rack's Out module as the channel's input: the rack plays on the channel, replacing hardware audio or MIDI (rack.list lists them); null takes a rack's Out off the input

parent_send.description: The implicit send to the parent buss/master (off: only explicit sends leave the track)

timebase.description: What this channel's items follow when the tempo changes (those that inherit it): project, beats, time or beats_position; they keep their place now

channels.description: 1-2: the track's main pair; up to 128 adds auxiliary channels 3-128 for routes and plug-in pins (a detector on 3/4, a multi-out instrument's outputs), outside the fader, pan and parent send

hw_output.description: Masters: the device outputs the main pair plays to: [l, r], [mono] or [] for none (engine.inputs lists them). Default: tr_0 [1, 2], other masters []

lane_mute.description: Masters: silence the master's own items (its prints) and nothing else

chain_midi.description: What the FX chain does with MIDI: bus (default; plug-ins hear and feed it in order) or instrument (only the first plug-in with a note input hears the track's MIDI; plug-ins' note output goes nowhere)

name: transport_play
title: Start playback from the current position.
description: Start playback from the current position. See describe for errors and examples.

name: transport_seek
title: Move the play position (one of seconds, beat or bar).
description: With master playrate enabled, prepare file-source converters off-thread before publishing the audible seek. Existing playback and live monitoring continue until ready; preparation errors leave the old seek epoch intact. See describe for errors and examples.

name: transport_stop
title: Stop playback and return to where it started (ends a recording).
description: Stop playback and return to where it started (ends a recording). See describe for errors and examples.
